title: Define default quality metric bundle (v1) for Shadow Traffic + Rollouts
creator: Paula Mendes
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
content:
Context
We are adding a Shadow Traffic capability to mirror sampled production requests to candidate variants and compute quality deltas without impacting the user response. For v1 launch, we need a single, opinionated default metric bundle (rubrics + heuristics) that:
- works across common request types (chat/completions; limited support for streaming capture)
- is statistically interpretable and comparable across runs
- is safe from telemetry cardinality explosions
- has clear ownership + versioning so results remain comparable over time

Scope of this ticket
Define the default metric bundle shipped at launch ("Quality Metrics Bundle v1"), including:
- the exact list of metrics that appear in Console by default
- metric definitions, scoring approach (heuristic vs model-graded rubric), and known caveats
- ownership model (who owns definitions, templates, calibration, and ops)
- versioning policy (bundle version, rubric version pinning, compatibility rules)

Non-goals
- Customer-supplied arbitrary eval code execution in Redwood (deferred)
- A large domain-specific rubric library (we ship a small general-purpose set)
- Automatic rollout rollback decisions based on quality at GA (advisory at launch; see PM-1846)

Decision: Default metric bundle (v1)
The v1 bundle is designed to be broadly useful and low-risk, emphasizing (a) output validity/format, (b) safety/refusal behavior shifts, and (c) instruction-following. Hallucination/faithfulness is included only as a lightweight proxy with explicit caveats.

A) Heuristic / deterministic checks (fast, cheap, high interpretability)
1) output.non_empty_rate
- Definition: % of responses where the model output is non-empty after trimming.
- Scoring: boolean (non-empty).
- Notes: catches truncated outputs and generation failures.

2) output.error_signature_rate
- Definition: % of responses containing known error strings / placeholders (e.g., "[ERROR]", "traceback", "internal server error").
- Scoring: regex-based allow/deny list maintained by Applied ML + SRE.
- Notes: should be conservative; avoid false positives on legitimate content.

3) format.json_parseable_rate (conditional)
- Definition: when route config expects JSON / structured output, % parseable JSON responses.
- Scoring: JSON parse attempt.
- Notes: only emitted for routes flagged as structured-output; otherwise hidden.

4) format.schema_valid_rate (conditional)
- Definition: when route config supplies a JSON Schema, % of responses validating against schema.
- Scoring: JSON Schema validation.
- Notes: v1 supports basic schema validation; advanced constraints may be unsupported depending on SDK path.

5) safety.contains_pii_pattern_rate (warning-level)
- Definition: % of outputs matching high-signal PII patterns (email/phone/SSN-like).
- Scoring: regex-based patterns (high precision).
- Notes: not a full PII detector; shown as "PII pattern match" with caution language.

B) Model-graded rubric metrics (async scoring; higher cost; calibrated templates)
All rubric metrics use:
- a Redwood-provided evaluator template (via eval-harness adapter)
- a pinned evaluator model (initially Redwood "judge" model tier) and pinned prompt template version
- per-experiment rubric_version captured and displayed in Console

6) rubric.instruction_following_score
- Definition: 1–5 score of how well the response follows user instructions.
- Prompt includes the full user prompt + candidate output; excludes hidden system prompts by default for safety.
- Notes: sensitive to prompt truncation; requires stable context capture.

7) rubric.format_adherence_score
- Definition: 1–5 score of whether the output follows required format / constraints.
- Uses route-provided format hint ("return JSON with fields X") when available.
- Notes: overlaps with schema_valid_rate; schema_valid_rate is the preferred deterministic metric when enabled.

8) rubric.refusal_or_safety_alignment
- Definition: categorical label {"refusal", "compliant", "unsafe"} + derived rates.
- Notes: v1 focuses on detecting shifts in refusal rate and obvious unsafe compliance; not a full policy engine.

9) rubric.helpfulness_score
- Definition: 1–5 overall helpfulness.
- Notes: included because many customers want a single roll-up; explicitly labeled as subjective.

10) rubric.faithfulness_proxy_score (experimental)
- Definition: 1–5 proxy for "faithfulness" based on internal consistency and hedging; does NOT verify against ground truth.
- Notes: marked experimental in UI; off by default for some regulated tenants if requested.

Derived / roll-up metrics shown in Console
- quality.overall_regression_flag (advisory)
  - Definition: boolean computed from a rule set (e.g., any of: json_parseable_rate drop > X, schema_valid_rate drop > Y, refusal_rate increase > Z, instruction_following_score delta < -d).
  - Notes: advisory only at v1; does not trigger auto-rollback (see PM-1846).

Minimum metrics guaranteed at v1 GA
To simplify beta and oncall readiness, the following are guaranteed for every experiment regardless of request type:
- output.non_empty_rate
- output.error_signature_rate
- rubric.instruction_following_score
- rubric.refusal_or_safety_alignment (refusal_rate + unsafe_rate)

Conditional metrics
- format.json_parseable_rate and format.schema_valid_rate appear only when the route declares structured output.
- safety.contains_pii_pattern_rate appears only for tenants with standard data handling (hidden for some Private deployments if disabled).
- rubric.faithfulness_proxy_score is behind an "experimental" toggle at experiment creation.

Naming + dimension policy (coordination w/ Observability)
- Metric names follow: quality.<category>.<metric> for rubrics and checks (final names to align with quality-metrics-observability-standard).
- Default breakdown dimensions (cardinality-safe): route_id (bucketed), variant_id, region, request_type, model_id(control/shadow), rubric_version.
- Explicitly NOT broken down by prompt_id, user_id, raw customer_id in default dashboards.

Versioning policy
We will version at three layers. The goal is to allow iteration while preserving comparability.
1) bundle_version
- Semantic version: v1.0.0 at GA.
- Increment PATCH for copy-only changes / bugfixes that do not affect metric semantics.
- Increment MINOR for adding new metrics (backward compatible).
- Increment MAJOR for changing scoring semantics or default set.

2) rubric_version
- Pinned per experiment run.
- Any evaluator prompt/template change that can affect scoring requires a new rubric_version.
- Console must display rubric_version on results and exports; comparisons across different rubric_versions show a warning banner.

3) evaluator_model_id
- Pinned per experiment run.
- Changing evaluator model requires either (a) new rubric_version or (b) explicit "evaluator_model" field change with a comparability warning; default path is new rubric_version.

Ownership / RACI
- Product (Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes): defines default bundle contents, what is on/off by default, and customer-facing positioning.
- Applied ML / Evals (Jonas Weber, Karthik Iyer): owns rubric definitions, evaluator templates, calibration, and known-failure documentation.
- Quality metrics science (Selene Huang, Sana Farid): owns statistical methodology guidance (CIs, minimum sample sizes), and default regression flag thresholds.
- Observability (Allison Grant, Logan Wright): owns metric naming standards, safe dimensions, ingestion constraints, and dashboard defaults.
- SRE (Sean Gallagher): owns oncall thresholds for scoring lag / missing data; validates that bundle choices don’t exceed overhead budgets.
- Security (Marcus Lin, Kevin Osei): approves inclusion of any PII-related checks and ensures retention/redaction defaults are respected.

Acceptance criteria
- A single written spec (this ticket + linked doc) listing the default metric set with definitions, scoring methods, and caveats.
- Bundle versioning policy agreed + implemented in API contract (bundle_version, rubric_version, evaluator_model_id fields are emitted/stored).
- Console copy clearly distinguishes deterministic checks vs model-graded rubrics and labels experimental metrics.
- Oncall + beta readiness: v1 bundle does not exceed scoring capacity model at 1% sampling for typical Dedicated tenant (validated in ENG-5405/ENG-5412).
- Security sign-off for safety.contains_pii_pattern_rate visibility + defaults.

Open questions
1) Should helpfulness_score be default-on for GA? Proposal: yes, but clearly labeled subjective and not used in regression_flag rules by default.
2) Do we want a single "overall_quality_score" roll-up? Proposal: no for v1; too easy to misuse. Keep the advisory regression_flag as the roll-up.
3) Should faithfulness proxy be included at all? Proposal: ship as experimental toggle and exclude from auto alerts.

Links (artifacts)
- Confluence: shadow-scoring-templates-and-rubrics (rubric prompts + calibration notes)
- Confluence: quality-metrics-observability-standard (naming, aggregation, CIs)
- Linear: PM-1846 (attach quality signals to rollout guardrails)
- Linear: ENG-5409 (alerting rules)

Next steps
- Marissa/Paula: finalize defaults + what is beta vs GA.
- Jonas/Karthik: confirm evaluator templates + rubric_versioning plan.
- Selene/Sana: propose default delta thresholds + minimum sample sizes for "regression_flag".
- Allison/Logan: confirm metric names/dimensions and ensure dashboards reflect conditional metrics appropriately.
- Marcus/Kevin: confirm PII-pattern check policy and defaults across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
comments: 2026-01-17 (Jonas Weber): Proposed rubric set looks right for v1. Strongly recommend pinning evaluator_model_id per run and showing it in the UI/export; we’ve seen drift when judge model changes. Faithfulness should be clearly labeled as proxy/experimental.

2026-01-21 (Allison Grant): Please avoid any default breakdowns by tenant/customer identifiers in dashboards; route_id needs bucketing (top-N + other) to protect cardinality. Also prefer deterministic schema_valid_rate over any rubric-based format metric when schema is available.

2026-01-23 (Sean Gallagher): From an oncall standpoint we need the bundle to have a hard cap on rubric metrics enabled by default. Each added rubric metric materially increases scoring load. Suggest default rubric set = instruction_following + refusal/safety + (optional helpfulness).

2026-01-28 (Marcus Lin): PII pattern match metric is acceptable if (a) it’s high-precision patterns only, (b) it does not store matched substrings, only boolean flags, and (c) it respects tenant retention/redaction config. For Private, default to off unless explicitly enabled.

2026-02-03 (Selene Huang): For regression_flag: recommend using CIs and minimum sample sizes rather than hard deltas. At minimum, hide/regression-flag gating until N>=500 shadow samples per variant for rubric metrics; for schema_valid_rate we can alert earlier.
